hero.label: ( 01 · Title Block )
hero.title: Adaptive math learning platform
hero.body: Mathua is an open-source adaptive math learning engine. You cannot advance until you have truly mastered the prerequisite, both speed and accuracy must be proven.

trust.label: ( 02 · Why it is trusted )
trust.body: Open-source under MIT. Sequencing inspired by Math Academy, with MIT OpenCourseWare and Art of Problem Solving consulted for curriculum structure and problem quality. Lessons build on OpenStax (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) and Algebrica (CC BY-NC 4.0). No accounts to start, no paywall on the graph.

mastery.title: Mastery gating
mastery.body: You cannot advance until your streak and response time both meet the threshold. Knowing the answer is not enough; you must know it fast.

graph.title: Concept graph
graph.body: Every concept is a node with explicit prerequisites. Mathua reads the graph and your progress together, and picks what you see next from the two.

spaced.title: Spaced repetition
spaced.body: Concepts you master resurface automatically before they decay. Reviews are woven into your session; there is no separate review mode.

states.label: ( 04 · The States )
states.scheduler: The scheduler enforces three hard rules: prerequisites must be mastered before a concept unlocks, the same concept never appears twice in a row and roughly 70% of each session is new material.

coverage.label: ( 05 · What Mathua covers )
coverage.note: Problems are generated on demand, never stored. There is nothing to memorise.

faq.label: ( 07 · Questions, answered. )

account.q: Do I need an account to start?
account.a: No. Begin studying immediately — accounts are optional and only needed to sync progress across devices.

speed.q: Why does speed matter, not just accuracy?
speed.a: Fluency requires retrieval under time pressure. Knowing the answer is not enough; you must know it fast, or the foundation will not hold the next concept.

quiz.a: A mastery-check quiz verifies retention across your recent concepts before new material continues.

free.a: Yes — MIT licensed, with no paywall on the graph. Every concept and generator is in the repository.

faq.extendBody: Every concept is a JSON node. Every problem is a Go generator function. Every contribution goes through a graph validator that rejects cycles and orphaned nodes automatically.

intro.title: How Mathua Works
intro.body: The engine behind the learning: a technical explanation of the concept graph, student model, diagnostic algorithm, task selection and scoring system.

cta.ready: Ready to find your starting point?

conceptGraph.title: The Concept Graph
conceptGraph.p1: Mathua represents all mathematical knowledge as a directed acyclic graph (a DAG). Each node in the graph is an atomic concept: the smallest unit of mathematical knowledge that can be practiced and mastered independently. Each directed edge is a prerequisite relationship. If concept B has an edge from concept A, then A must be mastered before B is ever shown to the student.
conceptGraph.p2: The graph currently contains {concepts} spanning {domains}: from early Counting through Calculus, Linear Algebra and Topology.
conceptGraph.p3: The graph is stored as a flat JSON file: {file}, and is community-editable. A graph validator runs on every pull request and rejects the change if it introduces a cycle.

spaced.title: Spaced Repetition
spaced.p1: When a concept reaches MASTERED, Mathua immediately schedules its next review using a simplified SM-2 algorithm.
spaced.schedule:
first review:   1 day
second review:  3 days
third review:  interval × ease_factor
ease_factor: starts at 2.5
decreases by 0.2 on each failed review
minimum value: 1.3
spaced.p2: Reviews are never presented as a separate "review mode." They are woven into every session by the scheduler, which manages the 70/30 balance between new material and review automatically.

diagnostic.title: The Diagnostic Algorithm
diagnostic.p1: When a student first opens Mathua, they enter a Computerised Adaptive Testing (CAT) session. The goal is to find the student's starting point using as few questions as possible.

steps.sort: The concept graph is sorted topologically. The diagnostic builds a covering set from the graph roots and evenly spaced concepts.
steps.forward: If the student answers correctly within the time limit, the algorithm moves forward: it next tests a concept further along the prerequisite chain.
steps.backward: If the student answers incorrectly or exceeds twice the expected time, the algorithm moves backward: it tests a concept earlier in the chain.
steps.probes: The assessment continues with multiple probes per concept until the student's starting point is clearly established.
steps.record: The diagnostic records a starting mastery estimate for every concept the student passed through. Concepts answered correctly count as LEARNING. Concepts answered quickly and accurately count as conditionally MASTERED and are skipped in early sessions.

diagnostic.p2: The diagnostic test asks as few questions as possible. Without this algorithm, a naive assessment of {concepts} would require up to {questions}. The CAT approach, picking each question by information gain over a covering set, reduces this by roughly 94%.
diagnostic.p3: The diagnostic test can be retaken at any time from your profile. Retaking does not delete progress: it creates a new knowledge estimate that is merged with existing data, always preferring the more optimistic estimate so students are never penalised for reassessing.

scheduler.title: The Task Selection Algorithm
scheduler.p1: The scheduler runs after every question is submitted. It selects the next concept by computing a priority score for every eligible concept.
scheduler.p2: Three hard rules the scheduler enforces regardless of priority scores:

rules.prerequisites: A concept whose prerequisites are not all MASTERED is never surfaced.
rules.repeat: The same concept is never shown twice in a row.
rules.mix: The scheduler targets a session composition of 70% new and practicing material, 30% review.

scoring.p1: Mathua tracks two separate scoring systems:

generators.title: Generator-Based Problems
generators.p1: Every problem in Mathua is generated on demand by a parameterised Go function: a generator. There is no static question bank.
generators.p2: The {code} parameter scales operand size from 0.0 to 1.0. The scheduler passes a difficulty value based on the student's current mastery score.

grading.title: Expression Grading with SymPy
grading.p1: From algebra onward, answers are expressions: {examples} where numeric comparison is no longer sufficient. Mathua uses a mixed Go/Python grading system: the router dispatches nine grading types — six pure-Go graders — and mathematical equivalence for algebra, calculus, differential equations and trigonometry is handled by a Python subprocess running {sympy}, bundled into the production image.
grading.p2: The {router} selects the grader by {gradingType}. Concepts with type {symbolic}, {polynomial} or {expression} route to {gradeSymPy}, which runs a long-lived Python 3 subprocess. The production image installs SymPy (pinned) and fails the build if it cannot grade, so there is no fallback path.
grading.p3: The Go client sends JSON requests to the Python subprocess via stdin. SymPy parses both expressions into trees and checks equivalence with {check}. This catches identities that string or coefficient comparison never could:

measuring.title: Measuring Learning
measuring.p1: Every answer in Mathua writes one row to an attempt log: student, concept, correctness, elapsed seconds, timestamp. Nothing is sampled or aggregated at write time — every metric below is computed from that raw log, per student or product-wide.

firstPass.name: First-pass rate
firstPass.text: Share of concepts answered correctly on the very first attempt.

secondPass.name: Second-pass rate
secondPass.text: Share correct within the first two attempts — the recovery metric. A gap between first- and second-pass means material is learnable with feedback but not yet automatic.

attempts.name: Average attempts per concept
attempts.text: Mean attempts across concepts; falls as fluency builds.

retention.name: Retention
retention.text: Students active in two or more distinct weeks ÷ all students who ever attempted. A coarse cohort signal, not a week-over-week curve.

trend.name: First-pass trend
trend.text: Last week minus first week. Positive means accuracy improved across the observed window; noisy at small N.

measuring.figureAlt: First-pass and second-pass rates across all learners, with Math Academy parity markers
measuring.p2: These are usage metrics, not an efficacy claim: no control group, no randomisation. Compare within a student over weeks, not across learners at different frontiers — and always read a weekly rate alongside its active-student count, since a week with three attempts can show 0% or 100% by accident.
measuring.p3: The figure above refreshes weekly from the live product-wide log — read it with its sample size, which rides in the caption. Early numbers move a lot; that is normal, not a verdict. Your live per-student numbers are on your {profile}, and the full methodology with regeneration commands lives in {docs}.
